items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Rhonda Lee, Wellesley
notes:
Rhonda Lee, Wellesley, expressed concern related to the enforcement of smoking legislation and the general inconsistency of smoking legislation and the Region's Smoke-Free Housing policy. She identified that there have been numerous incidents of smoking and aggression near a housing building in the Township of Wellesley. She requested that the smoking distance be of twenty (20) meters to match comparable locations. 

The Committee requested that Staff meet with the delegate to provide information on the current smoking laws that are applicable in the Region of Waterloo and discuss potential remedial actions.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
CSD-IPP-25-001, 2025 Immigration Strategy and Immigration Partnership Update
notes:
Tara Bedard, Executive Director of the Immigration Partnership, introduced the presentation on the 2025 Immigration Strategy and Immigration Partnership. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. She provided some background information on the immigration partnership and stated that the Waterloo Region Immigration Partnership is a collaboration of public, private, and non-profit partner organizations working together to take action to enhance immigrant success and community prosperity. She also introduced Katherine Peterson, Manager of the YMCA Three Rivers, and Dauda Raji, Community Services Manager (Operations & Partnerships), at the House of Friendship.

Dr. Ernest Osei, Chair of the Immigration Partnership Council, thanked the Region for its ongoing partnership and investment in the Immigration Partnership. He highlighted the beneficial impact of immigration in the Region. He noted the importance of taking action to enhance immigrant prosperity through strategic policies and systems. He further highlighted that more than seventy (70) partner organizations are ready to support immigration in order to safeguard the Region's future and aligns with the Region's commitment to growing with care and overall economic development strategy. He also noted that immigration will assist in meeting the needs of the changing population by ensuring that local services and the workforce can continue to thrive and that the community can continue to grow. He identified the strategic priorities to ensure an inclusive community for immigrants which include gathering information and building organizational resilience.

Tracey Hare, Vice-Chair of the Immigration Partnership Council, requested the support of Regional Council for the 2025-2028 Immigration Strategy and stated that if Regional Council supports the strategy they will be seeking to delegate at all area municipalities in the coming months. She acknowledged that, although services have been maintained, there has been a significant impact due to the reduction in federal funding. The Immigration Partnership needs consistent and reliable funding in order to maintain and grow services to meet demands as 98% of Canadian population and labour force growth comes from immigration.

Dr. E. Osei also requested that the Committee support the Staff recommendation to endorse the immigration strategy.

Responding to the Committee, T. Bedard confirmed that the Immigration Partnership continues to search for alternative funding through the province, non-profit organization, and private sector. She noted that provincial funding was also reduced in 2021-2022. Regional Chair K. Redman further confirmed that the Region became partners with the Immigration Partnership following notice of the federal funding reduction as well as advocated to local Members of Parliament and the federal government with letters of support to no avail. T. Bedard also explained that currently area municipalities have not provided direct funding as the majority of the funding is provided by the federal government, the Region of Waterloo, and United Way Waterloo Region Communities. The Committee also noted that the Region provides office space at 99 Regina Street for Immigration Partnership staff to work in as well as area municipalities have donated staff time and their expertise.

In response to the Committee, T. Bedard confirmed that there have been several initiatives to engage the community on immigration to provide information and receive feedback on challenges. She also noted that the Immigration Partnership continues to establish and strengthen connections with various community organizations including organizations that may be considered 'grassroots'.

The Committee expressed support for the Immigration Partnership and the important impact that immigration has in Canada.

motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions, as outlined in report CSD-IPP-25-001, dated June 10, 2025: Endorse the Immigration Partnership’s community-developed Waterloo Region Immigration Strategy 2025-2028; and Be leaders in supporting the economic and social success of immigrants and advocate for appropriate federal and provincial policy and investments.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions, as outlined in report CSD-IPP-25-001, dated June 10, 2025:

  1. Endorse the Immigration Partnership’s community-developed Waterloo Region Immigration Strategy 2025-2028; and
  2. Be leaders in supporting the economic and social success of immigrants and advocate for appropriate federal and provincial policy and investments.
